  • Member Hilliard joins the meeting at 3:41 p.m.
  • Health Department staff Savana Doudar provides a presentation of the City
  of Long Beach Homelessness Strategic Plan Upddate. Members of the
  committee have questions regarding the finalized date for the strategic plan.
  • Savana provides an overview of the Strategic Plan and facilitated an activity
  to engage committee members in offering feedback and identifying any
  areas that may be missing.
  • The committee and staff engaged in extensive discussion about goals
  that have not been met. Committee members expressed a desire for more
  quantitative data to better asses progress.

3.  25-54238  Recommendation to receive and file updates from the Mayor’s Fund and Policy
  Subcommittee and the Continuum of Care (CoC) HSAC representative.

  A motion was made by Member Howat, seconded by Voting Member Killion,
  to approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  11 Bedy, Howat, Johnson, Lewis, Simmons, Sngiem, Lie, Hilliard, Killion,
  Scott, Russell
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 2 Chotiswatdi, Wood

  Policy Subcommittee
  • Member Sarah Bedy provided an update, the subcommittee will be reviewing
  the 2024-2025 Policy recommendations to determine any updates or
  revisions that can be made.
  • Once the updates have been made the subcommittee will present to the
  HSAC committee.
  Mayors Fund Subcommittee
  • Member Kimberly Lewis provided an update, the subcommittee is currently
  reviewing the MOU and Standard Operating Procedure (SOP), once the
  SOP is finalized, it will serve as a guide for subcommittee members in

  reviewing the Mayor’s Fund applications.
  CoC Updates
  • Health Department staff Jennifer Santana provided an update: the Board met
  last month, during which two new board members were approved to serve
  on the board. However, one member withdrew due to a conflict of
  interest. Staff and board members also discussed updates regarding the
  restructuring of the subcommittees and the collaboration with the Long
  Beach Coalition to co-host the General CoC meetings.

4.  25-54241  Recommendation to discuss and approve the meeting schedule for the Homeless
  Services Advisory Committee.

  A motion was made by Member Bedy, seconded by Member Howat, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  11 Bedy, Howat, Johnson, Lewis, Simmons, Sngiem, Lie, Hilliard, Killion,
  Scott, Russell
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 2 Chotiswatdi, Wood

  • Committee members have approved reducing the meeting duration to 2
  hours and shifting the meeting times for the Homeless Services Advisory
  Committee to 4:30-6:30 p.m. The meetings will still take place on the first
  Wednesday of each month.

5.  25-54240  Recommendation to receive and file the Homeless Services Bureau Staff
  Operations and Updates Report by Paul Duncan from the Health Department.

  A motion was made by Member Howat, seconded by Voting Member Killion,
  to approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  11 Bedy, Howat, Johnson, Lewis, Simmons, Sngiem, Lie, Hilliard, Killion,
  Scott, Russell
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 2 Chotiswatdi, Wood

  • Health Department staff Dalton Dorr provided the quarterly operations data
  report on the services and number of clients being served at the MSC,
  Mobile Access Center and Outreach. The committee and staff engaged in a

  Page 3 of 5
   HOMELESS SERVICES ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES
  WEDNESDAY, FEBRUARY 5, 2025
  1500 HUGHES WAY STE. C-300 LONG BEACH, CA 90810

  discussion regarding the data, and the committee requested additional
  information for the next quarterly update.
  • Bureau Manager Paul Duncan provided staffing and operation updates. He
  noted that the full report for the 2025 Homeless Count is expected to be
  released by the end of April 2025.
  • The initial government freeze had a temporary
  impact on accessing Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)
  related drawdown systems. Staff is closely monitoring the situation to
  prepare for any potential future freeze.
  • The MSC activated 65 beds for Inclement Weather Shelter on 1/7 in
  response to high winds and remained activated for fire and cold weather
  response through 2/1.
  • Bitfocus has begun the merger of our Homeless Management information
  System (HMIS) server into the Los Angeles Homeless Authority (LAHSA)
  HMIS server.
  • Long Beach has been awarded $1M in Emergency Solutions Grant (ESG)
  Rapid Unsheltered Survivor Housing (RUSH) funds. Long Beach will be
  working with other jurisdictions to align use of the funds.
  • Staff applied through the LAHSA Interim housing RFP for operational and
  service cost for ABC and 702. Staff plan to release their own RFP for a
  service provider that would operate those shelter beds on behalf of the City.
